title: The mouthpiece of the Pipe Nebula
caption: Barnard 59 in the Pipe Nebula, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: Barnard 59, Nebula, Pipe Nebula · constellation Ophiuchus · about 600 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #43 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This highly detailed picture features Barnard 59, a section of a vast dark cloud of interstellar dust known as the Pipe Nebula. Barnard 59 forms the mouthpiece of the pipe.

The Pipe is a dark nebula. Instead of glowing, it shows up as a shadow, because its dust is thick enough to block the light of the stars behind it. Clouds like this are cold and dense, the kind of places where new stars can eventually form.

The camera was the Wide Field Imager, mounted on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. It is so large that ESO strongly recommends the zoomable version to appreciate it fully, since much of the detail only emerges at full size. The filters used spanned visible light and the near-infrared. The caption offers few other details.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (62.87 x 58.81 arcminutes) and distance (600 light years), the frame spans roughly 11 × 10 light-years. Its light set out about 600 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and I filters, spanning visible light and the near-infrared. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared, invisible to the eye, and the long exposures reveal far more background stars than an eye could see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

alt: Barnard 59, part of the Pipe Nebula, a vast dark cloud of interstellar dust.
